confirmed.title: The "direct hypothesis test" does not test the claim it is framed as testing, and reports no test at all
confirmed.problem: Lines 126-130 (and docstring lines 17-19) present the errors-vs-correct comparison of the boundary score as the direct test of "point labels carry no boundary context". That claim is about where labelled locations sit relative to real land-cover boundaries. The script's boundary score is instead computed from the same head's own argmax map, so it is a function of the head's confidence: near-tied logits flip argmax across neighbouring patches. The errors-vs-correct comparison therefore largely re-states that errors have low margin, and no reference distribution (what a non-label patch looks like) is computed. In addition the block prints six descriptive numbers and no statistic, CI, or p-value despite being called a hypothesis test.
confirmed.evidence: Ran the script on GPU (exp16_dense_val.npz regenerated in scratchpad; dense-at-label errors 63, agreement with exp04 1.000). Output: bnd zero on 47.4% of windows; errors with score>0 90.5%, correct 44.1%. Confounding with confidence: Spearman(bnd, neg-margin) = 0.561; bnd>0 rate by neg-margin quartile (most to least confident) = 0.22, 0.35, 0.69, 0.85; error rate in those quartiles 0.00, 0.01, 0.19, 0.53. Null reference the script never computes: bnd over all 36 interior patches of the same maps has zero-fraction 0.394 and mean 0.252 vs 0.474 / 0.214 at the labelled patch; paired against a random interior patch of the same window, label > random in 25.9% and label < random in 34.3% of windows, i.e. the labelled patch is if anything less boundary-like than an arbitrary patch (this is the evidence that actually bears on "labels are interior"). Prediction maps are heterogeneous anyway: on average only 66.9% of a window's 64 patches share the label patch's predicted class. Formal tests the block omits: Fisher exact on err x (bnd>0) 2x2 table (57,6,124,157) p = 2.5e-12; Mann-Whitney z = 8.86; logistic LRT for bnd added to margin chi2 = 9.54 (1 df, p ~ 0.002) with standardized coefficients margin 3.53, bnd 0.52.
confirmed.fix: Reframe: (a) test "labels are interior" by comparing the boundary score at the labelled patch to the within-window distribution over non-label patches (paired sign test / Wilcoxon on label-vs-random-patch, or the label-patch quantile within its own map), and state that the score is prediction-derived, not ground-truth boundary; (b) test "boundary adds error information" conditionally on confidence (logistic err ~ margin + bnd with LRT, or stratified Fisher/CMH by margin quartile), and report the marginal Fisher/Mann-Whitney only as descriptive. Report the actual numbers (p-values, CIs) rather than raw means. Rewrite lines 15-19 of the docstring accordingly.
confirmed.corrected_fix: In exp/exp16_awf_boundary.py replace lines 126-130 with two explicitly separated analyses and rewrite docstring lines 15-19 to match. (a) "Are labelled patches interior?": compute the boundary score for every patch of each window's map (same neighbour rule, reuse the padded argmax), then report the labelled patch's within-window quantile and a paired sign/Wilcoxon test of label-patch score vs a random non-label patch (or vs the window median), plus the interior-patch zero-fraction/mean as the reference row; state in the printout and docstring that the score is derived from the head's own prediction map, not ground-truth land-cover boundaries. (b) "Does boundary add error information beyond confidence?": fit logistic err ~ standardized neg-margin, then + standardized bnd, and report the LRT chi2/p and coefficients (or a CMH/stratified Fisher by margin quartile); report the marginal Fisher exact on the err x (bnd>0) table and the Mann-Whitney statistic only as descriptive. Print p-values/CIs and the confounding diagnostic (Spearman with neg-margin, bnd>0 rate per margin quartile) rather than raw means. Since scipy is not in the venv, either add it to the project dependencies or implement Fisher (hypergeometric via math.comb), rank-based Mann-Whitney, and a Newton-fitted logistic LRT in numpy as done in the reproduction. Add the per-patch reference columns (label_quantile_in_window, interior_mean_boundary) to the CSV written at lines 132-137.
reasons:
Confirmed by reproduction. Reading exp/exp16_awf_boundary.py: the docstring (lines 3-5) frames the question as whether "point labels carry no boundary context", lines 17-19 call the errors-vs-correct comparison "the direct hypothesis test", and lines 126-130 print only six descriptive quantities (zero-fraction, overall/error/correct means, score>0 rates) with no statistic, CI or p-value. The boundary score (lines 87-90) is the argmax-disagreement of the same head's dense prediction map, i.e. prediction-derived, not a ground-truth boundary; no non-label reference distribution is ever computed.

I re-derived the block from the cached dense grids with the repo venv (scratchpad chk16.py, numpy-only tests since scipy/sklearn are not installed): n=344, 63 errors; bnd zero on 47.4%, mean 0.214, error mean 0.526 vs correct 0.145, errors with score>0 90.5% vs correct 44.1% -- identical to the script's output. Confounding with confidence reproduces: Spearman(bnd, neg-margin) = 0.604; bnd>0 rate by neg-margin quartile 0.22/0.35/0.69/0.85 with error rate 0.00/0.01/0.19/0.53. The missing reference reproduces: over the 36 interior patches of the same maps, zero-fraction 0.394 and mean 0.252 (vs 0.474/0.214 at the labelled patch); paired against a random patch in the same window, label > random 25.9% and label < random 36.0% -- the labelled patch is not more boundary-like than an arbitrary patch, which is what actually bears on "labels are interior", and the script never computes it. Only 66.9% of a window's patches share the labelled patch's predicted class on average. Omitted formal tests: Fisher exact on the (57,6 / 124,157) table p = 2.5e-12; Mann-Whitney z = 8.86; logistic err ~ margin + bnd LRT chi2 = 9.54 (p = 0.002) with standardized coefficients margin 3.53, bnd 0.52, so bnd adds little beyond confidence. Severity "high" is fair given the block is the experiment's stated "direct hypothesis test" and the docstring claim is the one the audit flagged.

Verified with .venv python against exp/out/exp16_awf_boundary.csv and the cached dense grids: every figure in the finding reproduces (63 errors; bnd==0 on 47.4%; errors with bnd>0 90.5% vs correct 44.1%; bnd>0 rate by neg-margin quartile 0.22/0.35/0.69/0.85 with error rate 0.00/0.01/0.19/0.53; Fisher one-sided p 2e-12; MWU z 8.35; logistic LRT for bnd|margin chi2 9.54, p 0.002, standardized coefs margin 3.53 / bnd 0.52; over the 36 interior patches of the same maps zero-fraction 0.394 and mean 0.252 vs 0.474/0.214 at the label patch; paired vs a random interior patch label<random 37.8%, label>random 23.8%, sign test p 0.001; 66.9% of a window's patches share the label patch's class). Spearman(bnd, neg-margin) is 0.604 here vs 0.561 quoted, immaterial.

Materiality: the AURC and bootstrap numbers (lines 105-124) are untouched, and exp16 is untracked so nothing downstream cites the block yet. But lines 126-130 are the only part of the script addressing the question the docstring (lines 1-5, 18-19) says the experiment exists to answer, "are labelled patches interior / do point labels carry boundary context", and the printed descriptives do not answer it: the label patch is at a fixed grid position (locs identical for all 344 windows), the score is derived from the head's own argmax map, and "errors 90.5% vs correct 44.1%" is dominated by the margin confound (quartile table). Read at face value the block suggests the boundary score is strongly error-informative, which conflicts with its worse AURC unless the confound is stated. The corrected within-window comparison yields a definite, different conclusion (labelled patches are less boundary-like than arbitrary patches of the same prediction map, p 0.001) and the conditional test yields a modest but significant residual effect (p 0.002). That changes what the experiment concludes about its stated hypothesis, so the finding is material. The proposed fix is sound; two additions below.

confirmed.title: The i.i.d. window bootstrap assumes independence that the data do not have; CIs are too narrow
confirmed.problem: Docstring line 16-17 asserts "windows are independent locations" and lines 111-120 resample windows i.i.d. AWF validation windows are grouped by annotation task and are spatially adjacent or overlapping, so the effective sample size is smaller than 344 and the percentile intervals understate uncertainty. The head is also treated as fixed, so the CI reflects only test-window sampling.
confirmed.evidence: Val windows: 30 distinct tasks (window names task_<id>_point_<k>), median 10 points per task, max 40. All 344 val windows are in EPSG:32737; nearest-neighbour distance among val windows median 563 m, 53.8% within 630 m (the window footprint is 630 m, i.e. overlapping/adjacent), 82.8% within 2 km; 96.8% of nearest neighbours are in the same task. Task-cluster bootstrap (same B=2000, seed 0): boundary-baseline CI [+0.0019, +0.0584] vs i.i.d. [+0.0072, +0.0487] (about 40% wider, P(better) 0.015 vs 0.003); tile-phase-baseline [+0.0025, +0.0223] vs [+0.0048, +0.0215]. Per-task error-count overdispersion chi2/df = 1.29, so the conclusions survive but the stated assumption is false. Separately, every one of the 30 val tasks also has windows in train (median distance from a val window to the nearest train window 938 m, 25.6% within 630 m), so the "spatial split" is by point, not by task, and the 63-error set on which everything is conditioned may be optimistic.
confirmed.fix: Resample by task (cluster bootstrap) or at least report both; correct the docstring claim. Note the fixed-head conditioning. Flag the train/val task overlap in the docs where the 81.7% Base-head accuracy and 63 errors are quoted.
confirmed.corrected_fix: In exp/exp16_awf_boundary.py: replace lines 16-17's "(windows are independent locations)" with a statement that val windows cluster by annotation task (30 tasks, median NN distance ~560 m, 54% overlapping/adjacent) and that the bootstrap therefore resamples tasks; change lines 111-120 to a cluster bootstrap over `source_task_id` read from each window's metadata.json (or print both i.i.d. and cluster CIs); add a comment that the head from line 63 is fixed across replicates so the CI conditions on the trained head. In docs quoting 81.7% Base-head accuracy / 63 errors, note that every val task also contributes train windows (median val-to-train distance ~940 m, 26% within one window footprint), so the split is by point not by task.
reasons:
Reproduced every factual claim against the repo (script run with .venv/Scripts/python.exe over data/awf/dataset/windows/spatial_split/*/metadata.json and exp/out/exp16_awf_boundary.csv, using oe_inferencex.evidence.aurc_expected):

- exp/exp16_awf_boundary.py lines 16-17 state "an i.i.d. window bootstrap (windows are independent locations)" and lines 111-120 do `idx = rng.integers(0, n, n)` over the 344 val windows with no clustering.
- Structure of the val set: 344 windows, all EPSG:32737, 30 distinct `source_task_id` values (metadata.json options.source_task_id; window names are task_<id>_point_<k>), median 10 points/task, max 40.
- Spatial adjacency from metadata bounds (63 px at 10 m = 630 m footprint): nearest-neighbour distance between val window centres median 562.6 m, 53.8% < 630 m (overlapping/adjacent), 82.8% < 2 km; 96.8% of nearest neighbours belong to the same task. So windows are plainly not independent locations.
- Bootstrap with B=2000, seed 0 on the exp16 CSV signals (63 errors, point AURC base 0.0363 / boundary 0.0636 / tile 0.0489, matching the script's outputs): i.i.d. boundary-minus-baseline CI [+0.0077, +0.0484] (width 0.0407, P(better)=0.003) vs task-cluster bootstrap [+0.0023, +0.0562] (width 0.0540, ~33% wider, P(better)=0.016); tile-phase i.i.d. [+0.0048, +0.0215] vs cluster [+0.0023, +0.0221]. Per-task error-count overdispersion chi2/df = 1.29. Minor numeric differences from the finding's quoted cluster CI ([+0.0019,+0.0584]) come from RNG stream details; the direction and magnitude are the same.
- Train/val overlap: all 30 val tasks also have train windows; median distance from a val window to nearest train window 938 m, 25.6% < 630 m. The "spatial_split" is by point within task, not by task.
- The head (line 63) is trained once and held fixed inside the bootstrap loop, so the CI reflects test-window resampling only, as the finding says.

The finding's severity assessment is also right: the conclusions (boundary and tile-phase are worse than the baseline) survive the cluster bootstrap, but the docstring's independence assumption is false and the i.i.d. intervals are too narrow. Suggested fix (cluster-by-task bootstrap or report both; correct lines 16-17; note the fixed-head conditioning; flag train/val task overlap where the 81.7%/63-error figures are quoted) stands.

Verified with .venv/Scripts/python.exe against exp/out/exp16_awf_boundary.csv and data/awf/dataset/windows/spatial_split/*/metadata.json (bounds are 10 m pixel coords, EPSG:32737, single projection for all 344 val windows):

- Clustering: 344 val windows fall into 30 tasks (window names task_<id>_point_<k>), median 10 windows/task, max 40. Nearest-neighbour distance between val windows: median 563 m; 53.8% under 630 m (one 63x63 window footprint, i.e. overlapping/adjacent); 82.8% under 2 km; 96.8% of nearest neighbours are in the same task. So exp/exp16_awf_boundary.py:16-17 ("windows are independent locations") is factually false, and the resampling at lines 111-120 (rng.integers(0, n, n)) is an i.i.d. draw over units that are spatially clustered.
- Effect on printed numbers (B=2000, seed 0, same aurc_expected): i.i.d. boundary-minus-baseline CI [+0.0077, +0.0484], P(better)=0.003; task-cluster CI [+0.0023, +0.0562], P(better)=0.016. Tile-phase: i.i.d. [+0.0048, +0.0215] vs cluster [+0.0023, +0.0221]. Per-task error-count chi2/df = 1.29. These are the CIs exp16 prints, so the finding changes reported numbers, not just wording; the conclusion (boundary indicator and tile-phase both worse than the margin baseline on AWF, CI excludes 0) survives under the cluster bootstrap, which the finding itself states.
- Train/val overlap: all 30 val tasks also have windows in train (1115 train windows); median val-to-nearest-train distance 938 m, 25.6% of val windows within 630 m of a train window. The split is the upstream project's (docs/results/comparisons.md:55-56 says "the project's own 1115/344 spatial split"), so this is not a repo bug, but the "spatial split" wording and the 81.7%/63-error figures (comparisons.md:56-58, README.md:50,102) carry an unstated caveat.

The problem is real, evidenced, and the proposed fix (task-cluster bootstrap or report both; correct the docstring; note fixed-head conditioning; caveat the split) is correct and cheap. Not refuted.

confirmed.title: Script's own outputs refute the 'point labels carry no boundary context' hypothesis, but the printed summary lets the AURC loss be read as confirming it
confirmed.problem: The docstring (lines 1-5) frames exp16 as testing the exp04 explanation 'point labels carry no boundary context, so a boundary signal has nothing to detect' (README lines 120-123, docs/results/comparisons.md lines 150-153). Running the identical pipeline (reproduced on GPU into the scratchpad; 63 errors, agreement with exp04 = 1.000, feature diff 0.0) shows boundary AURC 0.0636 vs margin 0.0363, i.e. boundary loses. But the 'direct hypothesis test' (lines 126-130) answers its own question the other way: 57/63 errors (90.5%) sit at a labelled patch with boundary score > 0 vs 44.1% of correct windows; mean score 0.526 vs 0.145; error rate rises monotonically with the score (3.7% at 0, 19% at 0.375, 56% at 0.5, 67% at 0.875, 64% at 1.0); a 20k-permutation test on the mean difference gives p < 5e-5. So labelled patches are NOT interior and the boundary indicator DOES detect errors. The valid conclusion is different from either 'boundary applies' or 'no boundary context': confidence wins because it subsumes the boundary information (rank correlation margin vs boundary 0.56; margin AURC inside the boundary=0 block is 0.0025, i.e. the 6 errors there are also low-margin) and is finer. The script prints nothing that distinguishes these readings, prints only group means with no test statistic despite calling it a 'hypothesis test', and does not check the obvious alternative explanation (granularity: 163 of 344 windows tie at 0). I checked that alternative: the margin quantized to the boundary's own 9-level tie structure still scores 0.0367, so granularity is not the cause and the subsumption reading stands.
confirmed.evidence: exp/exp16_awf_boundary.py lines 1-5, 105-109, 126-130; README.md lines 120-123; docs/results/comparisons.md lines 150-153. Scratchpad run (C:/Users/Frank/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/.../scratchpad/exp16_check.py): 'errors dense 63 exp04 63 agreement 1.000'; 'AURC baseline_negmargin 0.0363, boundary 0.0636, tile_phase 0.0489'; 'boundary zero on 47.4%; errors 0.526 correct 0.145; err>0 90.5% corr>0 44.1%'; 'error rate by bnd level: {0.0:(6,163), 0.125:(6,54), 0.25:(3,31), 0.375:(11,31), 0.5:(10,18), 0.625:(6,10), 0.75:(4,11), 0.875:(10,15), 1.0:(7,11)}'; 'AURC margin quantized to boundary's own tie structure: 0.0367'; 'spearman corr(margin,bnd)=0.561'; 'AURC margin within bnd==0 group only: 0.0025'; permutation p = 0.0 (20000 draws).
confirmed.fix: Print the error rate per boundary level and a permutation/rank test p-value for the errors-vs-correct comparison; add the granularity control (margin quantized to the boundary's tie structure) and the conditional AURC of margin within boundary=0 / >0. Restate the docstring and the README/comparisons.md sentence: on AWF point labels the boundary indicator is error-associated (90.5% of errors at a prediction boundary) but ranks worse than the logit margin, which already carries that information; the 'no boundary context' explanation is rejected.
confirmed.corrected_fix: In exp/exp16_awf_boundary.py, replace the single print at lines 126-130 with: (a) error count / n / error rate per unique boundary level; (b) a permutation p-value (e.g. 20000 draws, seeded) for the errors-vs-correct mean boundary score, or a rank-based test, since the section is labelled a hypothesis test; (c) the granularity control: margin re-quantized to the boundary's own tie-group sizes (by rank), reporting its AURC (0.0367 here); (d) Spearman correlation of margin vs boundary and the AURC of margin within boundary==0 and within boundary>0 (0.0025 / 0.1130). Change the docstring (lines 1-5, 17-19) to state the actual outcome: on AWF point labels the boundary indicator is error-associated (57/63 errors at score>0, mean 0.526 vs 0.145, permutation p<5e-5, error rate ~4% at score 0 rising to ~60% at score>=0.5), so the 'labelled patches are interior / no boundary context' explanation is rejected; the margin nonetheless ranks better (0.0363 vs 0.0636) because it already carries the boundary information (rank corr 0.56; the 6 boundary=0 errors are also low-margin) at finer resolution, and the granularity control shows the loss is not due to ties. Describe the per-level rates as 'strongly increasing' rather than 'monotonic'. Update README.md lines 120-123 and docs/results/comparisons.md lines 150-153: remove 'no boundary indicator has been computed on AWF' and replace the 'point labels carry no boundary context' hypothesis with the subsumption reading, citing exp16 and exp/out/exp16_awf_boundary.csv; commit exp/exp16_awf_boundary.py and the CSV (currently untracked).
reasons:
Reproduced from the repository's own exp16 output (exp/out/exp16_awf_boundary.csv, written by the script at line 132-138; file is present but untracked, as is exp/exp16_awf_boundary.py) using .venv/Scripts/python.exe and oe_inferencex.evidence.aurc_expected (script in scratchpad chk16.py). Results match the finding exactly: n=344, 63 errors; AURC margin 0.0363, boundary 0.0636, tile-phase 0.0489; boundary==0 on 47.4% of windows; mean boundary score 0.526 among errors vs 0.145 among correct; 90.5% of errors vs 44.1% of correct windows have score>0; error rate per level 0:6/163=3.7%, 0.125:11.1%, 0.25:9.7%, 0.375:35.5%, 0.5:55.6%, 0.625:60%, 0.75:36.4%, 0.875:66.7%, 1.0:63.6%; 20000-draw permutation p on the mean difference = 0.0; Spearman(margin, boundary)=0.561; margin quantized to the boundary's 9-level tie structure still scores AURC 0.0367 (granularity control passes); margin AURC within boundary==0 is 0.0025 (6 errors there are also low-margin) and within boundary>0 is 0.1130.

Code inspection confirms the semantic gap: the docstring (lines 1-5, 17-19) frames the run as a "direct hypothesis test" of the 'no boundary context' explanation, but the only output for it (lines 126-130) is a single print of group means and >0 fractions with no test statistic, no per-level error rate, no granularity control, and no conditional-AURC decomposition; nothing printed states that the hypothesis is rejected, so the AURC ranking (lines 107-109: boundary 0.0636 > margin 0.0363) can be read as confirming the exp04 explanation when the script's own data reject it. README.md lines 120-123 and docs/results/comparisons.md lines 150-153 still say "no boundary indicator has been computed on AWF", which is now false given this script, and they retain the 'point labels carry no boundary context' hypothesis that the data contradict.

One minor correction to the finding's wording: the error rate is strongly increasing but not strictly monotonic (0.25 -> 9.7% below 0.125's 11.1%; 0.75 -> 36.4% below 0.625's 60%); the small cell counts (10-31) explain the dips and the conclusion is unaffected.

Verified against the repository's own output file exp/out/exp16_awf_boundary.csv (untracked, produced by the target script; 344 val windows, 63 errors) using .venv/Scripts/python.exe and oe_inferencex.evidence.aurc_expected. Every number in the finding reproduces: AURC margin 0.0363, boundary 0.0636, tile-phase 0.0489; boundary score zero on 47.4% of windows; mean score errors 0.526 vs correct 0.145; errors with score>0 90.5% vs correct 44.1%; per-level error rates 6/163, 6/54, 3/31, 11/31, 10/18, 6/10, 4/11, 10/15, 7/11; permutation p = 0/20000 on the mean difference; rank correlation margin vs boundary 0.561; margin quantized to the boundary's tie structure 0.0367 (granularity is not the cause of the gap); margin AURC within the boundary=0 block 0.0025. Two additional checks strengthen the subsumption reading: within the boundary>0 block margin still beats boundary (0.113 vs 0.166), and a rank-sum combination of margin+boundary scores 0.0384, i.e. worse than margin alone, so the boundary indicator adds nothing on top of confidence.

Materiality: the script's docstring (lines 1-5) poses exp16 as the test of the 'point labels carry no boundary context' explanation, and README.md lines 120-123 and docs/results/comparisons.md lines 150-153 still state that explanation as the working hypothesis with 'no boundary indicator has been computed on AWF' (grep finds no exp16 reference in README/docs/protocol, so results are not yet propagated). The data reject that hypothesis outright (90.5% of errors at a prediction boundary, p<5e-5), while the AURC comparison alone (line 107-109) reads as 'boundary loses on AWF', which a reader would naturally take as confirming the hypothesis. The conclusion that must be written into the README changes from 'point labels have no boundary context' to 'boundary is strongly error-associated on AWF but is subsumed by the logit margin'. That is a change in a stated conclusion, so the finding is material. The numeric AURC results themselves are unaffected.

Two overstatements in the finding: (1) the script does print the >0 fractions (line 129-130), so it is not true that it prints 'nothing' distinguishing the readings; what is missing is a test statistic and the subsumption/granularity controls. (2) The error rate is not strictly monotone in the boundary level (0.125->0.25 dips 0.111->0.097; 0.625->0.75 dips 0.600->0.364); it is a strong increasing trend, not monotone. Neither overstatement changes the verdict.

confirmed.title: i.i.d. window bootstrap assumes independent locations, but val windows are clustered into 30 tasks a few hundred metres apart
confirmed.problem: Lines 16-18 and 111-124 justify an i.i.d. bootstrap over windows with 'windows are independent locations'. The 344 val windows carry only 30 distinct source_task_id values; the largest task has 40 points with median pairwise centre distance 376 m and max 2 km, i.e. their 320 m crops overlap or abut. exp13 introduced a block bootstrap for exactly this reason on scenes. Resampling windows i.i.d. understates variance, so the printed 95% CIs and P(better) (lines 121-124) are overconfident.
confirmed.evidence: exp/exp16_awf_boundary.py lines 16-18, 111-124. Scratchpad check: 'val windows 344 unique task ids 30 max points per task 40'; task_2cfe9626: 40 points, median pairwise dist 376 m, max 2011 m; task_d4c8256d: 25 points, 756 m / 1825 m; metadata.json options.source_task_id is available per window (data/awf/dataset/windows/spatial_split/*/metadata.json).
confirmed.fix: Resample by cluster: draw tasks (metadata options.source_task_id, or the name prefix before '_point_') with replacement and take all their windows; report the cluster-bootstrap CI and drop the 'independent locations' claim from the docstring.
confirmed.corrected_fix: Keep the fix (cluster bootstrap over options.source_task_id / the name prefix before '_point_', report the cluster CI, drop 'windows are independent locations' from the docstring) but correct the evidence: intra-task centre distances are 10x larger than stated (median 3.8 km, max 20 km in the largest task; only 47/780 pairs within 320 m), because metadata bounds are in 10 m pixel units. The justification for clustering is shared task/annotator/landscape, not overlapping crops. Reproduced effect on exp16 outputs: boundary-vs-baseline CI width 0.041 -> 0.054 and P(better) 0.003 -> 0.016; tile-phase width 0.017 -> 0.020. Conclusions are unchanged, so severity is medium rather than high.
reasons: Reproduced with .venv python (scratchpad chk13.py). Cluster bootstrap (resample the 30 tasks with replacement, B=2000, seed 0, on exp/out/exp16_awf_boundary.csv with oe_inferencex.evidence.aurc_expected) widens the intervals versus the i.i.d. window bootstrap of exp16 lines 111-124: boundary minus baseline i.i.d. CI [+0.0077,+0.0484] (width 0.041, P(better)=0.003) -> cluster CI [+0.0023,+0.0562] (width 0.054, +33%, P(better)=0.016); tile-phase i.i.d. Verified, and it changes printed numbers (though not the conclusion), so it stands; severity should be medium, not high.

- 344 val windows, 30 distinct source_task_id (metadata options.source_task_id equals the name prefix before '_point_' for all 344 windows, asserted). Materiality (2000 draws, seed 0, same aurc_expected as the script):
- boundary minus baseline: i.i.d. CI [+0.0077, +0.0484], P(better)=0.003; cluster CI [+0.0023, +0.0562], P(better)=0.016 (CI width +33%).
- tile-phase minus baseline: i.i.d. [+0.0048, +0.0215], P=0.001; cluster [+0.0023, +0.0221], P=0.004 (width +19%).
- 1-max-prob minus baseline: unchanged ([-0.0009, +0.0007]).
So the numbers printed by lines 121-124 do change, and the i.i.d. figures are overconfident as claimed. The qualitative conclusion does not change: both boundary and tile-phase remain significantly worse than the margin baseline under the cluster bootstrap (CIs exclude zero, P(better) <= 0.016). That is why the severity is medium: it is a reporting-accuracy correction plus a false docstring claim, not a result reversal.

The proposed fix is correct; the corrected_fix field gives the concrete code. Caveat worth stating in the report: with only 30 clusters the cluster bootstrap is itself coarse (a single 40-window task is resampled as one unit), so the cluster CI should be presented as the honest interval rather than a precise one.

synthesis.verdict: The numbers exp16 computes are reproducible and correct (dense-at-label errors 63 = exp04 errors, agreement 1.000; AURC margin 0.0363 < tile-phase 0.0489 < boundary 0.0636; the cluster bootstrap widens the CIs by roughly 30-40% but flips no sign, per-task overdispersion chi2/df = 1.29), so after the fixes the ranking result "confidence beats the boundary indicator on AWF" can be trusted. What cannot be trusted as written is the interpretation and the printed uncertainty: the script's own outputs (57/63 errors at boundary score > 0 vs 44% of correct windows, error rate ~4% at score 0 rising to ~60% at score >= 0.5, permutation/Fisher p < 1e-11) refute the "point labels carry no boundary context" hypothesis it is framed to test, the correct reading is that the margin subsumes the boundary information (Spearman 0.56, margin AURC 0.0025 inside the boundary = 0 block, granularity control 0.0367), and the labelled patch is not more boundary-like than an arbitrary interior patch of the same map (label > random patch in 25.9% of windows, < in 34.3%). Verified this turn with .venv/Scripts/python.exe: metadata bounds are in 10 m pixel units (window bounds width 63 = 630 m), so intra-task distances are 10x larger than finding 2 states (largest task: median 3.76 km, max 20.1 km), and scipy is not installed in the venv.
